spec: Remove duplicate email addresses from a list. Email comparison should be case-insensitive.

inputs.note: Empty list tests the base case; no duplicates to remove.
Exact case duplicate; comparison is case-insensitive, so only one should remain.
Mixed case duplicate; first occurrence's casing is preserved.
Three entries with two case variants and a true duplicate; verifies dedup and order.
All three are case-insensitive duplicates; only the first is kept.
Different local parts (dot vs underscore) are not the same email; both should be retained.
Trailing and leading whitespace in some entries; these are treated as distinct strings unless the spec trims. Included to test whether whitespace is considered
No duplicates at all; output should equal input order.
Four entries all resolving to the same case-insensitive key; only the first is kept.
Multiple duplicates of both exact and case-variant forms.
Plus-addressing; the local part includes the tag. These are typically treated as different emails unless the spec ignores tags.
Email with quoted local part versus unquoted; these are different strings and likely different addresses.
Mixed duplicates across two distinct addresses; verifies that separate identities are not conflated.

def remove_duplicate_emails(emails: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """
    emails: A list of email address strings, possibly with duplicates and mixed case.
    returns: A list of unique email addresses with case-insensitive duplicates removed.
             The first occurrence of each email (preserving original case from the first seen instance)
             is retained, and the relative order of first occurrences is maintained.
    """
    seen: set[str] = set()
    unique: list[str] = []
    for email in emails:
        lowered = email.lower()
        if lowered not in seen:
            seen.add(lowered)
            unique.append(email)
    return unique

questions.text: Should leading or trailing whitespace around an e‑mail address be ignored when checking for duplicates?
questions.why: If whitespace is trimmed, "user@example.com " and " user@example.com" would be considered the same address as "user@example.com", changing the output for inputs that contain spaced variants.

options.label: Implementations treat the raw string, keeping spaces as part of the address.

questions.text: Should the function reject strings that are not syntactically valid e‑mail addresses?
questions.why: The current behaviour accepts any string (e.g., "Hello World", "A-b_c d") as an e‑mail; validation would drop or error on such entries, altering results for non‑email inputs.

options.label: All strings are accepted unchanged; no validation is performed.
Validate each entry against an e‑mail regex and discard or raise on invalid ones.

questions.text: Should e‑mail addresses be canonicalised beyond case‑insensitivity (e.g., ignore dots in the local part or treat "user+tag" as "user")?
questions.why: Many mail providers treat "user.name@example.com" and "username@example.com" as the same address; the current code treats them as distinct, so any future requirement to merge such variants would change deduplication results.

options.label: Only lower‑casing is applied; no further normalisation (dots, plus‑tags, quoted local parts) is performed.
Apply provider‑specific normalisation such as removing dots and stripping plus‑tags before comparison.
